item.title: Nostalgia as lullaby
item.description: We have a ten-month old baby at home, and each night we hold her and sing lullabies or hum to her until she falls asleep in our arms. Our favorite is “Island Child” (Korean: 섬집아기). It’s about a baby that falls asleep listening to the sound of the wave, while her mother is out tonging for oysters in the bay. But since the baby can’t tell if a song is an actual lullaby or not, sometimes I just sing to her songs that I like, even if it’s not a lullaby. She still falls asleep because it’s really our voice that calms her, not the song.

item.title: About
item.description: This is a simple blog where I post diaries of about my daily life. It mostly revolves around oddities of New Jersey suburban life.

item.title: Birds come in three
item.description:
First we found a fledgling in our driveway. At first glance, we couldn’t tell what kind of a bird it was. The feathers had a blueish hue and he was about the same size as a common grackle. We had a freak storm the day before, and the baby bird must have fallen out of the nest prematurely.

There was no cover for him on the driveway, so I gently held him and placed him under my neighbor’s shrubs in the shade. It was then the crows began to crow above me and I realized that this fledgling must have been their baby. It was so small though, and it seemed unlikely that he would survive off the nest.
